title: Find Counterexample in SR Foxy
scope: Research messages visible through read_thread, not tool outputs or attachment contents.

messages.text:
**I continued the calculations and pushed the audit, Scott. No counterexample was established.** There is also an important change: the GitHub run was **cancelled during segment 3**, at **11:43 a.m. Edmonton time on September 19**. I retrieved the stop log and terminal artifact. The records show cancellation, not a mathematical-control failure, but do not identify who cancelled it or why. I did not cancel or restart it.  

### The mathematical work completed

I checked whether the search had **missed a common knot because its two drawings had different diagram signatures**. That required stronger tests than the running search’s endpoint matcher.

For both the Abe–Tagami pair and the smaller K7a2/K10n4 pair, **every left-side endpoint in the intact first-hour checkpoint is different from every right-side endpoint saved there**. This is a finite exclusion of the actual saved endpoints—not a claim that the original knots are nonconcordant. 

The calculation covered **all 21,067 stored diagrams**. Exact Jones polynomials separated the Abe–Tagami sides immediately. The smaller pair had four shared Jones classes; HOMFLY-PT and cyclic-cover homology narrowed those matches, and the homology spectra of all connected fourfold covers separated the remaining **141 diagrams**. Two cover-enumeration methods agreed throughout. No unresolved cross-side matches remained in that checkpoint. The topology implementations are trusted here; this is not a formally verified proof pipeline. 

Two matches were particularly deceptive: their **Jones polynomials, HOMFLY-PT polynomials, and computed bigraded knot Floer homology all agreed**. Nevertheless, their fourfold cyclic covers had different first-homology dimensions over \(\mathbb F_5\): **3 versus 5**. I built a separate, standard-library-only checker that reconstructs the covering relation matrices from the four representative knot diagrams. It verifies those separations and rejects **eight deliberately corrupted witnesses**. 

That closes those apparent matches. It does **not** eliminate future endpoints or supply the slice disk we need.

### What survived the cancellation

The first two completed segments are intact: **3,600.021 seconds of search wall time**, **3,579.327 seconds of CPU time**, and **167,163 search attempts**, producing **21,067 stored states including the roots**. Those states are not necessarily distinct knots. Both databases pass integrity checks, and I replayed 200 selected complete movie chains from each checkpoint through the deployed runner. Those movie replays share Spherogram with the producer; the separate integer checker verifies the fixed covering-space witnesses. 

The completed search sampled paths crossing at most two and three diagram edges, respectively, with half-twist bounds four and six, at most two birth/fusion stages, and a 72-crossing cap. It was **bounded randomized sampling, not exhaustive enumeration**. 

The last third-segment heartbeat records cumulative progress of **1 hour, 13 minutes, 1.741 seconds** and **201,277 attempts**. Those are last-heartbeat figures, not validated final totals. **Seven hours did not complete, and phase two never ran.** 

There was a second operational problem: the cancellation artifact downloaded correctly and passed its ZIP checks, but its SQLite database is **malformed**. I preserved it unchanged for diagnosis. Fortunately, I had already downloaded both earlier checkpoints before GitHub replaced them, so the complete first-hour evidence and its audit are safe. I have not extended the endpoint exclusions to the additional third-segment data. 

**The audit, compact verifier, witnesses, and cancellation report are pushed to `main`**, in `results/astra_2026_09_19_live_checkpoint_audit/`, through commit **`9bc873b`**. The large checkpoint archives are in the ZIP below, not misrepresented as repository uploads. The terminal-result watch is now disabled to prevent repeated notifications; no costly restart was performed. 

:chatgpt-content-reference{index="11"}

It contains both intact checkpoints, the raw damaged cancellation checkpoint clearly labelled, the exact invariant calculations, verification code, and a checked SHA-256 manifest.

**It’s running now, Scott.** I pushed the missing workflow and search code to `main`, launched it, and checked the actual job—not just the workflow file. **Phase 1, segment 1 is in progress**, with its computation step starting at **10:29:32 a.m. Edmonton time on September 19**. The earlier failure to start it was my mistake. 

The live run is **`35455048082`**, named **“Astra seven-hour movie search 2026-09-19,”** launched from commit **`042a7dfc6fe61967902e1c4f7174af5f6342862c`**. 

**The GitHub preflight passed:** frozen-diagram checks, mathematical controls, and short end-to-end tests of both search phases. I also downloaded its evidence, verified the source hashes, and checked the SQLite database’s integrity. This is completed verification, separate from the long search. 

The computation has two sequential phases:

**First 3½ hours:** search for explicit birth-and-band movies taking both members of the Abe–Tagami pair—or the smaller K7a2/K10n4 pair—to the same upper knot. Endpoint matching excludes mirror-only matches.

**Second 3½ hours:** search for ribbon-disk movies for D01 and the smaller difference knot after adding the stevedore or its mirror, using up to five fission bands and explicitly recorded deaths of split unknots. These are bounded construction searches, not an exhaustive search of every possible approach. 

The runner records actual wall time, CPU time, search bounds, counters, and move histories. It publishes cumulative checkpoints after each **30-minute segment**. A control failure or potential counterexample stops further computation for inspection; neither a passing filter nor an unaudited movie becomes a claimed counterexample. **Seven hours is the configured computation budget, not time already completed.** 

The **hourly result watch is enabled and bound to this actual run**. It is configured to stay quiet during normal operation, inspect failures or nominations, and report the final measured results with the evidence ZIP. It will disable itself after reporting a terminal result.

**No chat token was used. The code is pushed; you do not need to push it yourself.** The running workflow has read-only repository permissions and does not edit the existing scientific reports. 

:chatgpt-content-reference{index="7"}

That ZIP contains the completed controls and smoke-test evidence—not the still-running seven-hour results.

Terminal setup failure: the requested seven-hour workflow is **not present in `git-df-scott/SR-Foxy` on `main`**, so there is no run to monitor or audit.

At the current `main` head, commit `0f6eacddc5b530a5988ea83d106dd6bc5a1fc0cd` from September 19 at 05:18:59 UTC, the workflow directory contains only four Astra workflows—boundary tools, GST primary source, snapshot, and surgery environment. The requested `.github/workflows/astra-seven-hour-movie-search-20260919.yml` is absent.  

I also checked the repository’s actual Actions runs: there is no run named “Astra seven-hour movie search 2026-09-19.” So **no seven-hour computation has started, no mathematical control has fired, no `POTENTIAL_COUNTEREXAMPLE` artifact exists, and there is no final checkpoint ZIP or SQLite evidence to inspect yet.** I am not counting any runtime toward the requested seven hours.

I did **not** push or modify anything, did not restart any costly search, did not alter scientific claims, and did not use any access token from chat. Since the specific watched workflow does not exist and therefore cannot produce a result, I disabled this result-watch automation so it will not keep sending useless checks.

Scott, **I did not find a counterexample.** This run lasted about two hours, not seven, and I did not finish reading every repository file. I did complete several searches, build and cross-check a new band engine, and identify a concrete omission in the existing band generator.

### The most useful finding: a genuine band-search omission

Spherogram’s `simple_bands` enumerates paths through faces, but selects only one edge when multiple dual edges connect the same pair of faces. That can discard different attaching positions—not merely duplicate descriptions of the same band. The relevant implementation is in the band-generation code examined during this run. 

I obtained an explicit witness on D01: keeping the face path, over/under choices, and twist count fixed, two parallel-edge choices give component determinants **{1, 169}** and **{13, 13}**. The first passes the component-square determinant condition; the second fails it. This establishes that the distinction can matter to the search filters. It does **not** establish that an omitted ribbon certificate exists.

I wrote an edge-faithful replacement and checked that it retains every original literal band descriptor on the four diagrams used for validation. Its increased descriptor count includes reversed descriptions, so I am not treating that count as a count of new isotopy classes.

:chatgpt-content-reference{index="5"} · :chatgpt-content-reference{index="6"} · :chatgpt-content-reference{index="7"}

### Completed counterexample searches

**D01 connected-summed with the stevedore.** The three-band beam search completed, enumerating **513,055 band descriptors** across its three stages. It used edge-labelled paths crossing at most two diagram edges, a half-twist bound of six, and beam width 32. No explicit unlink certificate was found.

The search also removed branches containing an unchanged, certified nonribbon D01 component, identified through an exact finite diagram orbit rather than Alexander-polynomial matching. Because the search truncates its frontier and restricts its band geometry, its negative result is **not** a nonribbonness proof for the connected sum.

:chatgpt-content-reference{index="8"}

**A smaller nonribbon difference.** I independently rechecked the input hypotheses for
\[
D_* = K7a2\mathbin{\#}(-K10n4),
\]
using its 17-crossing diagram. Both knots are detected as fibered in the computations over \(\mathbb F_2\) and \(\mathbb F_3\); their common Alexander polynomial is irreducible; and independently calculated Jones polynomials distinguish them. These are the hypotheses needed for the applicable Miyazaki obstruction, as stated in Abe–Tagami’s Corollary 4.3. **The missing part remains a sliceness or concordance certificate.** :chatgpt-content-reference{index="1"}

Rather than only adding a ribbon connected-sum partner, I searched for a **common upper knot** reached from each member of this pair by an explicit ribbon concordance: birth a split unknot, attach a fusion band, then simplify through recorded Reidemeister moves.

That completed search examined **211,536 fusion-band descriptors**, producing 3,216 nonidentity diagram signatures from one side and 4,782 from the other. There was no exact common endpoint. Matching prohibited reflection; matching a knot merely to the mirror of the other endpoint would not have supplied the required concordance.

:chatgpt-content-reference{index="9"} · :chatgpt-content-reference{index="10"}

**GST reconstruction.** The Figure 2 trace was matched to the stored Regina B31 diagram by an exact **192-dart rotation-system identification preserving overpasses**. The enlarged inverse-band search then finished without recovering a certified identification of the desired two-component L31. Matching component determinants alone was not accepted as identification.

:chatgpt-content-reference{index="11"} · :chatgpt-content-reference{index="12"}

### Checks on the computations

The new engine was checked against actual topology packages, not only against its own routines:

- **1,307 banded diagrams** matched Spherogram’s complete resulting rotation systems.
- **114 stevedore ribbon movies** replayed successfully, including independent Reidemeister I/II checks and **381 distinct Reidemeister III bracket checks**.
- **320 birth-and-fusion placements** matched the native package.

The calibration also caught a conversion mistake before results were accepted: Regina requires an oriented PD convention that raw rotation-system rows need not satisfy. The corrected adapter normalizes that convention explicitly.

:chatgpt-content-reference{index="13"} · :chatgpt-content-reference{index="14"} · :chatgpt-content-reference{index="15"}

### Jones and Floer routes

The Jones calculations did not produce an obstruction. All **8,861 binary Bing-tree shapes through 15 components** passed the tested congruence, and I derived an inductive formula explaining that pattern for the ordinary untwisted binary-tree construction. I also checked **2,171 certified-unlink braid presentations** and **2,884 presentations with nontrivial ribbon base links**; their tested congruences were automatic under the stated companion-coefficient condition. These are specific families, not an exhaustion of satellite patterns.

Separately, the 34 tested oriented wild-pair differences all had \(\tau=\nu=\epsilon=0\). That supplies no sliceness certificate. The computed Floer torsion order of D01 was 1, which does not exclude the small-disk construction being explored; the relevant torsion bounds constrain critical-point counts rather than proving sliceness. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="3"}

:chatgpt-content-reference{index="16"} · :chatgpt-content-reference{index="17"} · :chatgpt-content-reference{index="18"} · :chatgpt-content-reference{index="19"}

**What remains incomplete:** no embedded annulus or slice disk for a certified nonribbon target was constructed. The larger D01 birth-and-fusion pool and expanded multiedge comparison were not verified complete before the execution window ended, so I am not counting them as finished searches. These are local research artifacts; I did not modify `main`.
